hypotheses.short: Thermal mutual friction alpha(T), alpha(d) of a vortex dipole in a closed classical field, 0.14-0.95 T_BKT
hypotheses.statement: In the microcanonical projected GPE a single vortex-antivortex pair shrinks as d^2 = d0^2 - 4 alpha t with a friction alpha(T) that emerges from the field's own phonons; alpha rises monotonically from Shukla-Brachet-Pandit's low-T values to T_BKT, and its dependence on pair size (constant, ln d, or d^(2 eta)) is measurable.
hypotheses.rival: No resolvable shrinking (at T = 0 an isolated dipole does not shrink: Lucas-Surowka 2014), or shrinking dominated by imprint sound.
hypotheses.probe: Slope of d^2(t) on the finished dipole tracks (tracker pilots at 0.54 and 0.8 T_BKT, known-answer runs if finished): D = median slope significance (block jackknife).
literature: ShuklaBrachetPandit2014 (alpha only to 0.18 T_BKT, one grid)
Mehdi2022 (earlier microscopic modelling 'must be treated as phenomenological')
helium films: no parameter-free D(T) (Wu-Zhang-Zhai fit it)
Nam2012 / GroszekBillam2026: mobility ~ ln d or d^(2 eta) never measured on single pairs
hypotheses.lean_companion: dissipative dipole law on the torus (Zhu 2023 reduced law) as an ODE theorem: d^2 linear in t in the plane limit, with the periodic-image correction bounded

hypotheses.short: Einstein relation for a quantized vortex in a closed field: eta = alpha T / (2 pi rho_0)
hypotheses.statement: The diffusion of a vortex driven only by the field's own thermal phonons obeys the fluctuation-dissipation (Einstein) relation with the friction measured on the same trajectory.
hypotheses.rival: Diffusion far above the Einstein value, as measured by Neely et al. 2024 (eta ~ 100x the prediction, attributed to trap-wall vibrations).
hypotheses.probe: Structure function of the detrended pair separation on the existing dipole tracks: S(tau) = a + 4 eta tau; x = log10(eta/eta_Einstein); D = 2 / sigma_x (Einstein x = 0 against a 100x excess x = 2).
literature: Mehdi2022/2023 (the test is proposed as 'an important test of stochastic point-vortex theory')
Neely2024 (arXiv:2402.09920: eta 100x too large)
Reeves2022 (vortex-phonon coupling left open)
ThompsonStamp2012 (2D phonon drag with a fluctuation-dissipation relation)
hypotheses.lean_companion: Einstein relation as the stationarity condition of the Fokker-Planck operator of the stochastic point-vortex model (finite-dimensional algebraic identity)

hypotheses.short: Transverse friction alpha' (Iordanskii force) for bosons: do vortices move at the point-vortex velocity?
hypotheses.statement: Vortices in a thermal classical field move at (1 - alpha') times the torus point-vortex velocity induced by the other vortices, with alpha' resolvable between the two theoretical extremes 0 and rho_n/rho.
hypotheses.rival: alpha' = 0 (vortex moves with the superfluid) versus alpha' = rho_n/rho (Iordanskii-type); Shukla et al. could not put error bars on alpha'.
hypotheses.probe: Round-3 Part A vortex arms (eight imprinted vortices, positions every 10 time units): regression through the origin of measured displacement on the torus point-vortex prediction. Known answer at T = 0.115 (slope 1 within 0.15) gates the probe. D = (rho_n/rho)/SE(slope), the smaller of the two T ~ 0.45 arms.
literature: Iordanskii1964; Sonin1997; ThoulessAoNiu1996 (the transverse-force controversy: predictions from 0 to rho_n/rho)
ShuklaBrachetPandit2014 (alpha' sign-changing, no error bars)
Grani2025 (alpha' = 0.10-0.22 in a Fermi superfluid)
hypotheses.lean_companion: torus point-vortex Hamiltonian: conservation of the vortex impulse and of H under the Kirchhoff flow (no formal statement exists)

hypotheses.short: Equilibrium vortex matter is a Coulomb gas at the measured stiffness: pair-size law P(r) ~ r^(1-K)
hypotheses.statement: Below T_BKT the vortex-antivortex separation distribution of the thermal Bose field is a power law whose exponent is set by the independently measured stiffness K = 2 pi n_s/T (K at the scale r): the vortex positions alone give K (equivalently, the vortex temperature equals the bath temperature).
hypotheses.rival: The pair-size distribution is set by core structure and detection, independent of K.
hypotheses.probe: Nearest-opposite-sign distance distribution on r in [1.4, 6] in the 11 healthy large-box runs (K = 4.3-10.3): exponent a per run, then slope of a against K; D = slope/SE (rival slope 0).
literature: FanWilliams2022 (XY only, one asymptotic exponent, large errors)
Giorgetti2007; Foster2010 (pair function computed, no exponent analysis)
Choi2013 (law written, not testable)
ForresterChuWilliams (r^(-2 pi K) untested in a field simulation)
BoursierSerfaty2024-25 (rigorous dipole-length law)
hypotheses.lean_companion: pair collapse threshold and the scaling equation of state of the neutral 2D Coulomb gas (Salzberg-Prager / Hauge-Hemmer)

hypotheses.short: Josephson relation eta*K = 1 quantified on the torus: the 12-27 % offset is a geometry/window artefact
hypotheses.statement: With the exact Gaussian correlator of the periodic box (torus Green function) and a window beyond the pre-asymptotic range, the coherence exponent and the current-correlator stiffness satisfy eta*K = 1 within errors; the +12-27 % offset reported at L <= 64 does not survive.
hypotheses.rival: A persistent offset of order +0.2 (estimator bias, ensemble dependence or amplitude fluctuations).
hypotheses.probe: The five admitted L = 128 runs (C2): eta from ln g1 = c - eta G_T(r) on 8 <= r <= 32 of each final field, K from the run's current correlators; D = 0.2/SE(mean x), x = eta*K - 1; refuted if |mean x| > 3 SE.
literature: Foster2010; GawrylukBrewczyk2019 (graphical checks only)
Nazarenko et al. (finite-size Josephson form 20 % off)

BergerProkofevSvistunov2026 (ensemble-dependent stiffness at leading finite-size order)
hypotheses.lean_companion: Hasenbusch's two expressions for the Gaussian helicity modulus with winding sectors coincide (he 'checked numerically'): Poisson resummation of the theta sums

hypotheses.short: Last-pair equilibration: the box-scale vortex charge is one pair whatever the vortex number; time-resolved S_q(k_min) gives z and the equilibration-time law
hypotheses.statement: While a quench-born box-scale pair survives, |rho_q(k_min)|^2 sits on an O(1) plateau independent of the number of vortices in the box (80-440) and the stiffness is depressed; it drops by an order of magnitude when the last such pair annihilates. The distribution of that drop time over seeds and box sizes yields the dynamic exponent z where vortex-density estimators fail, and replaces Chu-Williams's continuous logarithmic recovery by discrete steps in a finite box.
hypotheses.rival: The box-scale charge is extensive (unscreened fraction of all vortices: |rho_q|^2 proportional to N_v), and the stiffness recovers continuously.
hypotheses.probe: ln |rho_q(k_min)|^2 against ln N_v over the seven depressed-stiffness runs: D = 1/SE(slope) (one pair: slope 0; extensive: slope 1); refuted if |slope| > 3 SE. Inputs partly seen in CLAIM-069.

Gazo2025 (time offsets fake exponents: the drop-time distribution avoids fitting a power law)
hypotheses.lean_companion: MatchingScreening.lean extended: a lower bound on |rho_q(k_min)| forces a pair of length >= L/(2 pi N); with the dipole law, a lower bound on the remaining equilibration time

hypotheses.short: Finite-k dielectric relation of a compressible superfluid: transverse response = vortex polarisation + phonon floor at every k
hypotheses.statement: At every wavevector, not only the lowest, the transverse current response of the thermal field is the point-vortex term n_eff^2 (2 pi)^2 |rho_q(k)|^2/k^2 plus a smooth phonon floor: a measured epsilon(k) for a compressible Bose field, for which no functional form exists.
hypotheses.rival: Beyond the lowest shells the transverse response is unrelated to the vortex charge structure factor (density-vorticity cross terms dominate).
hypotheses.probe: L = 192 snapshots, shells |m|^2 = 5, 8, 9, 10, 13, 16 (none used in CLAIM-069): Pearson r between the field's R_T(k) and the vortex-only R_T(k) over 36 (run, shell) points; D = atanh(r) sqrt(n - 3).

Foster2010; GawrylukBrewczyk2019 (k -> 0 extrapolation by fits of convenience)
stiffness review gap 3: no exact finite-k relation for a compressible fluid
VallatBeck1994 / Faulkner2017 (k = 0 polarisation term)
hypotheses.lean_companion: Fourier identity already in MatchingScreening.lean (pointVortex_norm_sq); add the bound S_q(k) <= (k a)^2 N for a gas of pairs of size <= a

hypotheses.short: Decay law of an imposed supercurrent on the torus: slip rate vs velocity, AHNS exponent 1 + K/2 against MWJO exponent K - 1
hypotheses.statement: The rate of thermal winding slips of a persistent current in a periodic 2D Bose field is a power law of the flow velocity whose exponent discriminates the two rival theories; pinning-free and barrier-free, which films and ring experiments are not.
hypotheses.rival: Rate independent of velocity over the accessible range, or no slips within feasible run times.
hypotheses.probe: A five-minute simulation: L = 32 thermal state (T ~ 0.79, K ~ 5.4) boosted to windings 1, 2, 3; slips counted every time unit; D = Poisson significance of the excess slip count at winding 3 over winding 1.
literature: helium review gap 3: a_AHNS = 1 + pi J/T vs a_MWJO = 2 pi J/T - 1, reconciled by Andersson-Lidmar as a size/boundary crossover; untestable in films (pinning)
GillisVolzMochel1989
Nottingham finite-velocity KT papers (unread: novelty capped at 0.6)
our round-3/4 accidental and imposed winding runs
hypotheses.lean_companion: TopologicalProtection.lean: winding changes only by integer slips; add the energy barrier of a pair crossing in a current-carrying state

hypotheses.short: Cutoff law of the classical-field BKT point: n_c lambda^2 = ln(380/g) + ln(E_cut/T), slope exactly 1 in ln E_cut
hypotheses.statement: The critical degeneracy of a Rayleigh-Jeans field with a sharp momentum cutoff is the Prokof'ev-Ruebenacker-Svistunov universal constant plus the ultraviolet logarithm ln(E_cut/T). It accounts for the 29 % excess we reported (and a 26 % offset in Nazarenko et al.) and predicts T_BKT = 0.92 at k_cut = 2 pi/3 and 0.67 at k_cut = 2 pi with no parameter.
hypotheses.rival: The naive quantum value ln(380/g) with no cutoff term (excess unexplained), or a non-logarithmic cutoff dependence.
hypotheses.probe: RETRODICTION on round-2 crossings (inputs known before registration): D = |x_H - x_rival|/sigma with x = n lambda^2 at the L = 64 crossing and sigma the full L = 32 -> 64 finite-size shift; refuted if the measured x is more than 3 sigma from x_H.

hypotheses.lean_companion: the conversion integral as a theorem: integral of [1/(e^{(eps+X)/T}-1) - T/(eps+X) on eps<E] d eps = T ln(T/E) + o(1) as X -> 0

hypotheses.short: Two-fluid sound from the closed field's own dynamics: a second branch in S(k, omega) at L = 192
hypotheses.statement: The density dynamic structure factor of the microcanonical field below T_BKT shows two propagating branches whose speeds follow Landau's two-fluid quartic with the model's own stiffness, comparable with Christodoulou et al. 2021 (data held).
hypotheses.rival: A single (Bogoliubov) branch plus a diffusive central peak at the available resolution.
hypotheses.probe: rho_k(t) on eight modes (|m|^2 = 4, 8, 9, 16) from the 100 snapshots (dt = 10) of each L = 192 run: periodograms in c = omega/k; D = median over runs of the robust significance of a second peak below 0.7 c1.
